models.section: 4 Model I: Adaptive Transportation Network Model
models.purpose: turn the Baltimore road network into a weighted directed graph
models.summary: The roads become a directed graph and each edge takes a weight from the entropy of three factors: flow, capacity and peak time.

variables.definition: the directed graph standing for the whole road network
the set of nodes read from nodes all.csv
the set of edges read from edges all.csv
the number of edges, given as 565496
the number of factors, given as 3
the j-th factor of the i-th edge
the raw factor scaled to the unit interval
the reciprocal of the logarithm of the edge count
the share of edge i in the standardized sum of factor j
the entropy of the j-th factor across the edges
the entropy weight of the j-th factor
the combined weight of the i-th edge

governing_equations.purpose: the road network written as a directed graph of nodes and edges
each factor scaled to the unit interval so the larger value marks the more important edge
the constant that scales the entropy, with n the edge count
the share of one edge in the standardized sum of one factor
the entropy of one factor across all the edges
the weight of one factor, larger where the factor spreads the edges apart
the weight of one edge as the weighted sum of its three standardized factors

equation_status.reason: displayed and read from the page raster

objectives: give the heavier weight to the road section that matters more
constraints: only the three chosen factors enter the weight

details: the network starts from the recorded edges and flows
flow in equals flow out once the collapsed bridge is removed

parameter_estimation.method: entropy weights from the spread of the standardized factors; the score weights are stated, not fitted

steps: read the nodes and the edges
scale each factor to the unit interval
compute the share, the entropy and the weight of each factor
combine the three weights into one edge weight
algorithm.convergence_criteria: none stated; the weights are a direct calculation

assumptions: the larger value of a factor marks the more important edge
the edge count is 565496 and the factor count is 3

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the weights are computed and mapped, but the three numbers are never printed

validation_refs: the weighted network is drawn in Figure 4 with a legend of weight bands
models.computational_cost: one pass over 565496 edges and three factors
strengths: the weights come from the data rather than from a guess
the weighted network is drawn so the darker roads are the heavier ones
limitations: the entropy treats every edge as one observation, so a short street counts as much as a long one
no printed check shows the three weights sum to one
missing_details: the numerical weights of the three factors are never printed

models.purpose: move the collapsed bridge's flow onto the two bridges above it and recompute the shortest paths
models.summary: The collapsed bridge is dropped from the graph, its flow is split between the two surviving bridges by capacity, and the shortest paths are recomputed.

variables.definition: the flow entering the i-th place
the flow leaving the j-th place
the shortest path distance from node i to node j
the set of paths from node i to node j
the weight of the edge from node i to node j

governing_equations.purpose: flow balance: what enters the network equals what leaves it
the shortest path distance after the collapsed bridge is removed

equation_status.reason: displayed and read from the page raster

objectives: keep the flow balanced after the bridge is removed
find the new shortest path between each pair of nodes
constraints: the diverted flow goes only to the two bridges above the collapsed one

details: the network starts from the recorded edges and flows
flow in equals flow out once the collapsed bridge is removed

parameter_estimation.method: entropy weights from the spread of the standardized factors; the score weights are stated, not fitted

steps: drop the edges of the collapsed bridge
split its flow between the two surviving bridges in proportion to their capacity
recompute the shortest path with Dijkstra
algorithm.convergence_criteria: the shortest path distance is the minimum over the surviving paths

assumptions: travel behaviour stays fixed in the short term
road capacity stays fixed during the analysis

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the rerouting is drawn but the diverted volumes are not printed

validation_refs: Figures 5 and 6 compare the flow before and after the collapse
models.computational_cost: one shortest-path pass over the surviving network
strengths: the before and after charts show the flow leaving the collapsed bridge and arriving at the other two
the commuting time is recomputed from the new paths
limitations: the split is described as proportional to capacity but no formula for the split is printed
the flow balance equates a sum over one index with a sum over another
missing_details: no table gives the diverted flow on each of the two bridges

models.section: 5 Model II: Upgraded Bus Network Model
models.purpose: rank the bus stops and group them so the shelters can be renovated or built where they are needed
models.summary: Stops are scored on ridership and shelter, grouped into five clusters, and each cluster is given a minimum spanning tree.

variables.definition: the raw ridership of a stop
ridership scaled to the unit interval
the longitude or latitude of a stop
position scaled to the unit interval
the combined score used to rank a stop

governing_equations.purpose: ridership scaled to the unit interval
longitude and latitude scaled to the unit interval
the ranking score, with the missing shelter coded as one
the shelter score, adding closeness to the city centre

equation_status.reason: displayed and read from the page raster

objectives: put the new and the renovated shelters where the score is highest
constraints: the score weights are fixed at the stated values

details: the network starts from the recorded edges and flows
flow in equals flow out once the collapsed bridge is removed

parameter_estimation.method: entropy weights from the spread of the standardized factors; the score weights are stated, not fitted

steps: fill the missing ridership by linear interpolation
drop the outliers beyond one and a half interquartile ranges
split the stops into five clusters and build a minimum spanning tree in each
algorithm.convergence_criteria: the minimum spanning tree connects every stop in the cluster at the least total edge weight

assumptions: a stop with high ridership and no shelter should be served first
five clusters are enough to separate the stops

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the ranking and the five trees are drawn, but the cluster count is not justified

validation_refs: Figure 11 ranks the stops and Figures 17 to 21 draw the five trees
models.computational_cost: one clustering pass and five minimum spanning trees
strengths: the ranking points at the stops that need a shelter most
the correlation of score with route count is checked with a heatmap
limitations: both score formulas state their weights without deriving them
the clustering method is named but not specified
missing_details: no criterion is given for choosing five clusters

models.section: 6 Model III: Integrated Multimodal Transport Model
models.purpose: read the bus and rail overlap and propose one new north-south rail line where the overlap is weakest
models.summary: The bus and rail networks overlap far more east-west than north-south, so one new north-south line is proposed with transfer facilities.

variables.definition: how far the bus and rail networks share the east-west direction
how far the bus and rail networks share the north-south direction

equation_status.reason: the proposal is read off the map and no equation is written for it

objectives: shorten the north-south commute by adding a rail line where the overlap is weakest
constraints: the new line stays inside the land network already modelled

details: the network starts from the recorded edges and flows
flow in equals flow out once the collapsed bridge is removed

parameter_estimation.method: entropy weights from the spread of the standardized factors; the score weights are stated, not fitted

steps: compare the bus and rail networks direction by direction
mark the north-south corridor where the overlap is weakest
propose one line there with transfer facilities
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not applicable; the proposal is read off the map

assumptions: a new line shortens the commute once the short-term disruption passes

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the proposal is argued from the map and no ridership or travel-time figure is computed

validation_refs: Figure 27 draws the overlap and marks the proposed line in red
models.computational_cost: a visual comparison of the two networks
strengths: the recommendation names the corridor and the transfer facilities
limitations: no equation fixes the line's route or its expected ridership
the disruption during construction is described but not measured
missing_details: the line is drawn but never given a length or a cost

dependency_edges.handoff: the edge weights are what the shortest path is measured in after the bridge is removed
the same road network carries the bus stops that are then ranked and clustered
the ranked bus network is what the rail network is compared against
